newsitem.title: UK: Stakis profits rise, confident about future.
newsitem.headline: Stakis profits rise, confident about future.

text.p: Scottish-based Stakis Plc on Monday announced higher annual results and said it was confident of the long-term prospects for its hotel, casino and leisure club divisions.

"We have a clear strategy to develop three businesses whose markets are expected to be buoyant in the middle term," chief executive David Michels said, announcing annual pre-tax, pre-exceptional profit 24 percent higher at 30.7 million pounds ($51.6 million).

"We have a management team capable of delivering growth in all those businesses. We have adequate and prudent financing for that growth. I look forward to the next few years with confidence and enthusiasm," he added.

The results for the year to end-September were in line with a forecast made by the company five weeks ago when it announced it was buying five Metropole hotels in Britain from Lonrho Plc for 327 million pounds.
The deal is being largely funded by a four-for-seven rights issue, at 82p per share, which will raise 222 million pounds.
The acquisition will increase the value of the group by nearly 50 percent. Gearing goes up to 45 percent after the purchase, from 38 percent at year-end.

Stakis said operating profit from its hotel division, 45-strong before the deal, rose 29 percent to 40.2 million pounds. Better occupancy rates and higher charges per room helped boost the division. New hotels are being built in London, Sheffield, Dublin and Belfast.

Profits from the company's 22 casinos fell by 2.8 million pounds to 8.9 million, a result which the company said was "disappointing". But it added that a review had identified this business as having great potential and Stakis intends to focus on provincial operations in Britain.

"We have achieved a great deal in the past six months and we remain committed to the casino division although it will be some time before we can realise its full potential," Michels said. ($1=.5953 Pound)
